title: Life is poker, not chess
coreMove: Commit under incomplete information while describing confidence as a range, not a verdict.
sourcePressure: The chapter makes poker the governing model for real decisions because information stays hidden and luck can separate a sound process from a single result.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not teach caution as waiting for full certainty; the lesson is deciding while naming what remains hidden.

sourceAnchors.name: chess board
sourceAnchors.detail: The source uses chess as the near-perfect-information contrast that misleads people about ordinary decisions.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A chess board offers the comfort of exposed pieces, but most real choices do not lay their facts out that politely.

sourceAnchors.name: poker hand
sourceAnchors.detail: The source uses poker as the structural model for hidden information, partial reads, and luck shaping a result after commitment.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A poker hand makes the missing information visible by refusing to show it.

sourceAnchors.name: I'm not sure
sourceAnchors.detail: The source reframes the admission as accurate reporting rather than weakness when the situation genuinely contains uncertainty.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: In an incomplete environment, the honest sentence is often the one that leaves room for what cannot yet be seen.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: orchard frost insurance purchase before blossom season
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a costly premium is bought without knowing the late-April frost pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel marks known bud counts, unknown night temperatures, and premium cost in separate columns before recommending a policy with a confidence range.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rows of closed apple buds shine silver in the cold before sunrise.

exampleSpecs.domain: indie game studio deciding whether to launch in early access
exampleSpecs.stakes: cash runs out if they wait, reputation suffers if hidden bugs dominate release
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille tells the team which bugs are visible, which player reactions remain hidden, and what launch size preserves a chance to learn without pretending the board is complete.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 9:18 p.m., Camille watches the bug tracker refresh beside the payroll runway spreadsheet.

exampleSpecs.stakes: too few staff risks patient waits; too many staff empties a strained budget
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Tell me what we do not know yet," Sophie says, then separates booked vacations, flu trend uncertainty, and agency-nurse cost before making the call.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Tell me what we do not know yet," Sophie says, tapping the holiday roster.

exampleSpecs.domain: museum exhibit attendance forecast before a traveling show opens
exampleSpecs.stakes: printing too many catalogs wastes money; printing too few misses revenue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pavel states a 60-75 percent range for the catalog order and names the hidden variables instead of giving the board a fake exact number.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Fresh catalog paper snaps under Pavel’s thumb as the board waits for one clean number.

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal snowplow route redesign before the first storm
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wrong routing model strands side streets and exposes the city to complaints
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars moves from defending one perfect route map to showing three route options with assumptions written directly on each map.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Lars one storm season to stop calling a route map finished.

exampleSpecs.domain: student exchange placement choice with incomplete host-family information
exampleSpecs.stakes: a student must choose a placement before every variable about fit can be known
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You help Isabel state what she knows, what remains hidden, and what decision rule she will use if the missing information stays missing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You have three host profiles open and none of them answers the question Isabel most wants answered.

skillTargets: separate luck from skill without flattening either
state confidence as ranges under incomplete information
